title: From 5G to NearLink: Europe’s Next Digital Dependency Risk - The Wire China
gist: Less than a decade after confronting reliance on Huawei/ZTE for 5G, Europe is drifting into a new, harder-to-detect dependency on NearLink (SparkLink/星闪), China's homegrown alternative to Bluetooth and WiFi, which is already entering the continent via imported smartphones and wearables.

themes.theme: A second Chinese connectivity-standard dependency for Europe

insights.claim: Europe is drifting into a new dependency on Chinese connectivity technology that the article frames as more diffuse and harder to detect than the earlier Huawei/ZTE 5G equipment reliance it confronted less than a decade ago.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A recurring pattern of Chinese-standard infiltration into European telecom/connectivity infrastructure suggests investors should watch for a second wave of EU security reviews and potential restrictions targeting embedded short-range wireless chips, not just headline 5G network gear.
insights.quote: Less than a decade after Europe had to confront the risks of relying on Huawei, ZTE and other Chinese telecom equipment makers for its 5G networks, it is drifting into a new dependence that is more diffuse and harder to detect.

insights.claim: NearLink (also called SparkLink, 星闪), positioned as China's alternative to Bluetooth and WiFi, is already entering the European market embedded in imported smartphones and wearable devices.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A Chinese-controlled short-range wireless standard gaining embedded distribution in consumer electronics sold in Europe creates a chokepoint risk analogous to the 5G equipment episode — worth tracking for which device makers and chipmakers are adopting NearLink and whether EU regulators respond.
